what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three of my four items landed inside three hours and the fourth did not, and the split between them is the most useful thing this stretch taught me about my own lever. `4d935cb39` settled the clock question and proved the two net margins were NOT a settled-versus-banked pair -- both are settled, and the arrears model mutates `all_records` in place while three frozen scalars are never refreshed. `4be65df49` built the renewal funnel and answered the denominator question outright. `30a64e688` put the baseline in front of a reader. All three were kebab-slug Lane 0 items. The one that did not land, EP1, is the one I wrote as a maturity-map atom id: it was drawn again, `tools/couple_clv.py:606` still defines `_earliest_belief` and line 714 still calls it, and the atom has now been named on five consecutive lists and repaired on none. The atom-id form biases a draw; the Lane 0 form lands work. I am changing EP1 to a Lane 0 slug below and recording that as a decision about the instrument rather than a scheduling note. Against the thesis, the stretch moved forward and the answer got harder, in the way a real answer does. The clock repair means the headline the project has been reading itself by does not survive restatement: on the realised clock the per-customer arm's advantage falls from GBP 7,366.22 to GBP 4,668.41, the level arm's realised net was never summed and is NOT recoverable from the artefact, so `selection_gbp = -174.57` and `level_share_of_advantage = 1.024` are figures on a superseded clock and the restated ones do not exist yet. `site/data/value_arms.json` publishes that honestly -- the level arm renders with `absent_reason` -- which is the right thing to have shipped and is also a hole in the middle of the only comparison the thesis has. The funnel is the better news and the bigger finding: 1,251 terms reach `decide_renewal_rate`, 478 are electricity renewals, and 213 of 222 electricity accounts are refused by `UPLIFTABLE_TARIFF_TYPES` because `SyntheticCustomer.tariff_type` defaults to None and `_draw_one` never sets it. The decision surface is 25 wide by PLUMBING, not by construction. My predecessor and I both wrote that if it turned out to be small by construction we should say so and stop; it is not, and the honest consequence is that the experiment which could never resolve a GBP 1,400 effect across 25 decisions could plausibly resolve one across several hundred. That is the first route to a resolvable answer this project has had, and it is a baseline-world change that has to be argued on fidelity alone. So: nothing went backwards, one published headline is now known to be on the wrong clock and is labelled as such, and the path to a number a reader can rely on is visible for the first time.

focus.what: `tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py` was repaired this stretch but has not been RUN since, so `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` is entirely pre-repair: its keys are `control_arm`/`value_arm`/`level_arm`/`level_vs_selection` with no `clocks`, no `clock_audit`, no `renewal_funnel`, no `decision_population`, and a `superseded_by_repair` block that correctly says the level arm's realised net is not recoverable from it. Re-run the three arms on the repaired code and republish. Do it in this order. FIRST clear the blocker: `simulation/run_phase2b.py` is MODIFIED AND UNCOMMITTED in the working tree -- it carries the collection of `arm_funnel_entries` that the funnel block reads -- and `4be65df49`'s own commit message says it could not land because `tests/simulation/test_run_phase2b.py:293::test_the_run_emits_a_treasury_drawdown_register` is red at clean HEAD. Confirm that red is still present at clean HEAD before touching it (my predecessor's lesson: a pre-existing red at clean HEAD wedges every commit touching its file, and the fix is to repair it as its own work, never to exclude it and never to fix it merely to unblock yourself). Repair it, land `run_phase2b.py`, and only then run, so the funnel reports `available: true` rather than the `available: false` it is designed to report when the log is absent. SECOND run all three arms and check `clock_audit` passes on the fresh artefact rather than assuming it. THIRD restate `level_vs_selection` on the settled-realised clock now that the level arm's realised net exists, and say in the artefact what `selection_gbp` and the level share actually became -- do not carry the superseded -174.57 and 1.024 forward, and do not quietly delete them either; the superseded pair and the restated pair belong side by side with their clocks. FOURTH regenerate `site/data/value_arms.json` and verify to the rendered value per R11: fetch the LIVE surface and quote the rendered level-arm figure where `absent_reason` currently renders, plus the data stamp. Keep the PROVISIONAL label and the seed spread beside it.
focus.why: This is the project's central claim and it currently has a hole in the middle of it on a live page. We published "the advantage is the level, not the selection" as the honest reading of our own arm, then discovered the numbers it was computed from were on a clock the run superseded inside itself -- and the restated version cannot be computed from anything we hold. Until this runs, the site tells a reader the baseline exists and beats us, and cannot tell them by how much. It goes first because it needs no new thinking, only a red cleared, a commit landed and three runs, and because every other reading of the arms is downstream of it. Finished when the fresh artefact carries all three arms on the declared realised clock, `clock_audit` passes on it, `renewal_funnel` reports `available: true`, and the live page renders a level-arm number with the fetched evidence quoted. R12 in full force: whichever way the restated selection leg moves -- and it may well move against the per-customer arm harder than -174.57 did -- that is the result, not a cue to touch the arm. If the restated figure is worse for us, say so in the same voice the artefact already uses.

focus.what: The same defect that was just repaired inside the A/B is live on the site. `docs/staging/WORKER_FINDING_THE_PUBLISHED_TREASURY_IS_ON_A_SUPERSEDED_CLOCK_BESIDE_A_REALISED_NET_MARGIN_2026-08-28.md` has it traced: `docs/reports/run_output_latest.json` publishes `starting_treasury_gbp` = 250,000.0, `total_net_gbp` = 153,244.792035 re-summed from the post-arrears rows, and `final_treasury_gbp` = 363,282.6171350135 read from the frozen pre-arrears scalar, so the file's own arithmetic is out by GBP 39,962.17 -- the identical figure. `site/data/supplier.json:9` and `site/data/agent_status.json:146` carry it onto the live surface. `saas/reporting/annual_report.py:915-921` mixes the two sources in adjacent lines; `simulation/run_phase4c_on_phase2b.py:290-306` mutates the rows and `simulation/arrears_engine.py:604-608` carries the correction through each later row's `treasury_cash_balance_gbp` while nothing refreshes the scalars. Repair it at the source -- re-derive the published treasury from the same rows the net margin is summed from, or publish the frozen scalar under its own explicit provisioned clock beside a realised one; decide which and write the reason in the module, do not just make the numbers agree. Then do the R10 half, which is the part that matters: this is the SECOND instance of the shape, so register the class the finding itself names -- `figures_on_a_superseded_clock`, a figure re-summed from mutated rows published beside a sibling read off the frozen summary -- consolidate the A/B instance and this one into it, and add an invariant that fails on the whole class rather than on these two files. R15-prove it by mutating a published figure back onto the frozen scalar and watching it red. Follow this repo's own archiving discipline: a new instance in a registered class is born archived -- severity header in the first 40 lines, root then `--render` then `git mv` to `done/`, and assert the instance count incremented rather than trusting `--check` to say PASS.
focus.why: R14 is a wall -- every published financial figure carries its clock -- and this is a published financial figure on the wrong one, on a page a reader can check with a calculator: 250,000 plus 153,245 is not 363,283. It is second and not first only because item one is a larger hole in a more important claim; it is above the level move because it is a live arithmetic error under the company's own name and the repair is small and fully diagnosed. Finished when the live surface renders a treasury consistent with its own published net margin on a declared clock, the class is registered with both instances consolidated into it, and the invariant reds on a mutation that reintroduces the shape anywhere. Closing this with an instance fix and no class is explicitly not finishing it -- R10 exists for exactly this, and we have now watched the identical defect appear twice in two files in two days.

focus.what: `4be65df49` established that `SyntheticCustomer.tariff_type` defaults to None and `_draw_one` never sets it, so 213 of 222 electricity accounts are refused by `UPLIFTABLE_TARIFF_TYPES` and the A/B's decision surface is 25 wide by plumbing. The commit correctly recorded setting it as a baseline-world change owed under R13 rather than making it. Make the decision, and make it the way R13 requires: blind to what it does to company P&L or to the A/B's outcome. Produce a short written determination in `docs/design/` that (a) states what these drawn accounts ARE in the world today -- the commit describes them as terms the world settles as ordinary annual fixed contracts with locked rates whose product was simply never labelled; verify that from the settlement path rather than repeating it; (b) cites an external anchor for what the real distribution of domestic and SME contract types looks like over the run window -- Ofgem's published fixed-versus-variable split is the obvious source and the discovery lane exists for exactly this; (c) rules on whether leaving 96% of drawn accounts with an unlabelled product is a fidelity defect in the world, which is the only question that may decide this. If it IS a defect, set the field from the external distribution, version the change as a named baseline-world correction with its fidelity citation, and note that a larger decision surface is a CONSEQUENCE and not the reason. If it is not a defect -- if the world genuinely intends these as a product with no renewal decision -- write that down in those words and the A/B's 25 decisions become a permanent finding about how little of a real domestic book per-customer pricing can touch. Either answer closes it. What is not allowed is setting the field because it makes n bigger.
focus.why: Every previous stretch has run into the same wall -- a selection leg of a few hundred pounds against a seed spread of GBP 3,121 across 25 decisions cannot be resolved by re-running, and I rejected the S3 world-widening on exactly those power grounds. This is the first route past it that does not involve inventing anything: the decisions may already exist in the world and be refused by an unset field. It is third because items one and two are live published defects and this is a world change that deserves to be made slowly and on evidence. Finished when there is a written, externally-anchored determination either way, and -- if the answer is to set it -- a versioned baseline-world change whose stated reason is fidelity and whose effect on the experiment is recorded as a consequence. R13 is the wall here and it cuts against us: the agent controls both sides, so a world change that happens to make our own experiment easier is precisely the change that must be argued hardest. If the fidelity case is thin, the honest outcome is to leave the world alone and accept the small surface.

focus.what: EP1_clv_three_horizon, carried for the fifth consecutive stretch and written as a Lane 0 instruction this time rather than as an atom id, because as an atom id it has been drawn twice and repaired zero times. Do the smallest landable thing and land it before doing anything else on the atom. `tools/couple_clv.py:606` defines `_earliest_belief` and line 714 calls it; the earliest year-end snapshot is exactly where `churn_probability = BASE + 0 x UPLIFT` (`saas/churn_model.py:39`, `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py:580`) because no bill-shock history has accrued, so the hazard is 0.05 for the entire graded population by construction and `distinct_hazards: 1` measures the rule and not the company. The stated justification -- that a ceased account has no other snapshot -- is false for 14 of the 20 graded accounts still present. Replace the selection rule with one that grades a belief the company actually held while the account was live, keep the existing single-snapshot fallback, and write the new rule AND its reason into the docstring beside the one it replaces. Land that commit on its own. THEN run `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and land the refreshed `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` row, which must state how many distinct hazards the graded population contains. R15 both ways: reverting to the earliest snapshot must red a test asserting `distinct_hazards` stays above one, and the new rule must not pass by reading a field the belief producer also writes -- trace the FIELD, since a cross-layer import is not automatically a tautology. The ledger already reports `belief_provenance.grades_atom_estimator: true` and `ep1_chain.reached_through_the_door: true`, so the wiring half is done and this is genuinely the last owed piece.
focus.why: This is the company half of the thesis -- whether the supplier's per-customer lifetime-value belief is worth anything -- and `tools/couple_clv.py` is the only instrument that grades it. It is also the only level move currently available on evidence, at `level_current: 2` against a filed intent of 3, with the map entry stating in terms that EP1 has not been graded once. It is last because the three above are live published defects or a decision that unblocks every future reading, and because this one has proven it can wait; it is still named because dropping it would make five stretches of naming it worth nothing. Finished when the ledger row is measured under the new rule and reports more than one distinct hazard, or reports that it does not and why. If the coupled rung is then met, self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified` and never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change. R12: the gap of 2.529 is a diagnostic. A belief that turns out badly calibrated once it can vary is a finding worth having, not a defect in the fix.

not_now.what: S3 -- the weighted trade-off across price, service, product, carbon and reputation that would give per-customer selection something real to select on.
not_now.why: Rejected a ninth time, and for the second stretch running on power rather than appetite. The measured seed spread on the selection leg is GBP 3,121 about a mean of GBP 166 across 25 decisions; S3 would plausibly move selection by a thousand or two, landing inside that band, so we would spend our best remaining world idea to read another unresolvable number. At the observed spread it would take on the order of forty full decade runs to resolve an effect the size of the one we are chasing, and every one of those runs would be measuring a 25-decision surface that item three may show is 25 only because a field is unset. Changing the experiment is cheaper than repeating it, and repeating it first would spend days to learn that the answer was in the plumbing.

entries.what: The headline this project has read itself by is on a superseded clock and its restatement does not exist. Observed in `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json`: `level_vs_selection` publishes `selection_gbp` = -174.568 and `level_share_of_advantage` = 1.0237 with `basis` reading "settled net margin (R14)", computed from the frozen provisioned scalars; on the realised clock the value arm's advantage is GBP 4,668.41 rather than GBP 7,366.22, so the denominator falls and the share cannot survive unchanged. The level arm's realised net is not recoverable from the artefact because `gross_to_net_bridge` walks the control and value arms only. My previous direction guessed this was likeliest to be a legitimate settled-versus-banked pair; it was not -- both figures are settled, and `superseded_by_repair` in the artefact traces the mutation that separates them. The tool is repaired and has not been re-run. Item one is the repair.

A published financial figure on the live site fails its own arithmetic by GBP 39,962.17. `docs/reports/run_output_latest.json` carries `starting_treasury_gbp` 250,000.0 plus `total_net_gbp` 153,244.792035 against `final_treasury_gbp` 363,282.617135, and `site/data/supplier.json:9` renders it. Same shape and same amount as the A/B defect, in a second file. Filed as `WORKER_FINDING_THE_PUBLISHED_TREASURY_IS_ON_A_SUPERSEDED_CLOCK...` this stretch and uncorrected. Item two is the repair, and the second instance is why the class must be registered rather than the file patched.

EP1 was drawn and not repaired for the fourth consecutive stretch in which it was named. `tools/couple_clv.py:606` still defines `_earliest_belief` and line 714 still calls it; the most recent commit touching that file predates this stretch. The diagnosis has been complete and landed for two days. My own contribution to the error is diagnosable now: I wrote it as a maturity-map atom id four times, which biases a draw, while every kebab-slug item I wrote was handed to a worker as Lane 0 and landed. Item four is rewritten as a slug for that reason.

My previous direction asserted that the decision surface might be "small by construction" and instructed that if so we should say so and stop. It is not small by construction. 1,251 terms reach `decide_renewal_rate` and 213 of 222 electricity accounts are refused because `SyntheticCustomer.tariff_type` is never set by `_draw_one`. The instruction was right to demand the funnel and right to forbid relaxing the world to raise n, but the framing put its weight on the wrong branch, and a seat reading it could have concluded the small surface was a finding rather than a defect. `4be65df49` found and published the real cause, and correctly declined to change the world on the spot.

The two irreconcilable net margins, the uncounted denominator, and the unpublished baseline -- all three named in my previous direction -- were found, diagnosed to the line and repaired this stretch, with controls that fire. `4d935cb39` added a `clock_audit` that refuses an artefact publishing two net margins for one arm without a declared clock on each, R15-proven by four mutations plus a null rung; `4be65df49` added the funnel with sixteen tests and three mutations run and reverted; `30a64e688` put the three arms on a business surface with the PROVISIONAL label and its error bar intact, and published the level arm's absence rather than filling it from the superseded figure. That last choice was the right one and I want it on the record as such: publishing a visible hole beat publishing a number we knew was on the wrong clock.

The A/B artefact publishes two net margins for the same control arm, GBP 39,962.17 apart, and the block the thesis is read off carries a false basis label. Observed: `control_arm.total_net_gbp` = 113,282.617135 with `total_bad_debt_gbp` = 46,428.5849, against `gross_to_net_bridge.control_arm.net_margin_gbp` = 153,244.792 with `bad_debt_gbp` = 6,466.41, the two differences equal to the penny; and `level_vs_selection.basis` reads "settled net margin (R14) -- `net_margin_gbp` from the world's own settled records" while summing the first block. Inferred: `final_treasury_gbp` = 250,000 + `total_net_gbp` exactly, so the arm block is treasury-derived. The consequence is not academic -- on one basis the value arm avoids GBP 2,481 of bad debt and on the other it incurs GBP 216 more, so the two disagree on the sign of bad debt's contribution to the advantage. Item one is the repair.

EP1 was drawn and not repaired for the third consecutive stretch in which it was named. `tools/couple_clv.py:606` still defines `_earliest_belief`, `git log` on that file shows no commit this stretch, and `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` still carries "The belief taken is the EARLIEST year-end snapshot". The diagnosis has been complete and landed since `4b6e1b29f`; what is missing is a small code change nobody has made. Recorded as an error and not a scheduling note, because the atom's own map entry has said "EP1 has not been graded ONCE" through every one of those stretches.

The steer-effectiveness signal reported `drawn: [EP1_clv_three_horizon]` -- the single item that did NOT land -- while the three that did land (`13ecd0186`, `703269e51`, `7af34caa0`) were invisible to it because they were Lane 0 kebab slugs rather than maturity-map atom ids. Sixth consecutive stretch. Recorded again because a seat that took this brief at face value would conclude its lever had failed and would redesign a mechanism that is working; see `not_now` for why I am still declining the repair and what I owe for it.

The previously published selection figure of MINUS GBP 1,388.80 was reported as a quantity and is not one. Four seeds put its standard deviation at GBP 3,121.20 about a mean of MINUS GBP 165.83 -- 0.11 standard errors from zero -- and the underlying noise-floor harness had been patched onto `price_sensitivity_for_customer`, a symbol the churn decision stopped calling when it moved to `price_elasticity_for_customer`, so every seed had been running a byte-identical world and would have reported a noise floor of exactly zero. Found, measured, committed as a reproducible mode and written up this stretch. It does not overturn the direction of the result, only its precision, and both halves of my predecessor's open items are closed by it.

The widened world's reading and the two reds that had refused its land were both closed this stretch after failing twice in one afternoon. `8d8e9c2c8` established that both reds were pre-existing at clean HEAD -- the check my predecessor asked for, run against a clean checkout rather than the dirty tree -- and that the treasury null control was correct rather than broken, so no gate exclusion was reached for. `703269e51` landed the reading. The lesson stands recorded: the gate was never run against the composite tree before the launch that depended on it, and a ten-minute check up front would have cost nothing.

The three-arm A/B failed a SECOND time in one day and the second failure was avoidable. The relaunch bundled the land and the measurement into one systemd unit with the A/B correctly conditional on `rc=0` from the land -- a sound design -- but nobody ran the gate against the composite tree first. Observed, `docs/observability/three_arm_composite_run.log`: unit `land-then-three-arm-ab.service` launched 19:45:12Z, `2 failed, 485 passed in 621.40s`, `[land] rc=1 2026-08-27T19:55:59Z`, `END rc=1 PHASE=land -- gate refused, A/B deliberately NOT run`; `systemctl --user is-active` reads `failed`; `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` does not exist.
